brief: A seven-cell honeycomb work surface, covered on top, with every open outside edge finished with caps.

requirements.requirement: Seven hex bases forming a honeycomb work surface (one centre cell with six around it)
requirements.evidence: Seven full hex bases: centre (0,0) plus six at (-1,0),(-1,1),(0,-1),(0,1),(1,-1),(1,0), level 0. Joint bolts on the six centre walls lock them; check_build clean, meshClash clear.

requirements.requirement: The work surface is covered on top
requirements.evidence: Seven top covers (cover family, face top), one on each base.

requirements.requirement: Every open outside edge is finished with a cap
requirements.evidence: 18 caps (cap family) on the 18 open outside edges of the seven-cell flower, three per ring cell; no OPEN_CAP_FACE issue reported.

finish.summary: Built a seven-cell honeycomb work surface: seven full hex bases in a flower, a top cover on every cell, six joint bolts locking the ring to the centre, and 18 caps on all outside edges. check_build reports no issues and meshClash is clear.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
